messages:
anna_dev: Hey team — customer corp-x reports intermittent 600-1200ms tail spikes on the embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings. Happening ~3-4x/day, only on the us-east route.

sara_support: Any error codes or correlation ids? Model / request sizes?

anna_dev: Model: open-embed-1024-q4, route: embeddings-prod-us-east-1. Most requests are tiny (1-5 tokens) but occasionally a single huge doc (~3500 tokens) goes through at the same time. Example request ids: rJ12, rJ13, rK99.

mike_sre: Could be dynamic batching coalescing small + huge into one GPU batch causing mem pressure + kernel switching overhead. Do we see KV cache evictions / coldstart around spikes?

anna_dev: We pulled a short trace. Notice when the large request enters, the batcher expands and runtime does a big allocation; prefetched KV gets evicted causing latency on next few requests. Paste of condensed runtime log:

```
[2026-02-28T14:02:31Z] dynbatch: flush batch size=128 (small-heavy mix)
[2026-02-28T14:02:31Z] runtime: model open-embed-1024-q4 select_kernels=opt1
[2026-02-28T14:02:31Z] runtime: kv_cache: mem_used 6.2GB -> 8.7GB (grow)
[2026-02-28T14:02:32Z] runtime: kv_cache: evict_count=1 reason=mem_threshold
[2026-02-28T14:02:32Z] cpu: paging 1
[2026-02-28T14:02:32Z] request rK99: served in 890ms
[2026-02-28T14:02:33Z] request rJ12: served in 1100ms (waiting for kernel select + kv warm)
```

sara_support: Oof. Any embeddings dimension errors in the logs? Customer mentioned some 512 vs 768 weirdness before.

anna_dev: Not in this thread. We did see one `embedding_dim_mismatch` on a different day when a client switched to a smaller variant, but today is pure tail latency, not dim mismatch.

ben_ml: Two hypotheses: 1) dynamic batching allows wide size variance in one flush, causing huge memory spike and forcing eviction (and kernel recompile for that seq_len); 2) cold workers get allocated different quantization kernels for big seqs, increasing latency. Quick mitigation: reduce `max_batch_size` and enable `batch_stride_limit` or set `prefer_homogeneous_batches=true` for embeddings route.

mike_sre: Agreed. We can also enable a tiny prefilter which prevents >1024-token requests from joining small-request coalescing. That would isolate big docs to a dedicated slot.

anna_dev: Repro steps I used locally (minimal):

1) run a flood of 1-3 token requests at 500qps to route A.
2) inject a single 3500-token request into same route.
3) observe dynbatch flush with mixed seqs and tail latency spike.

curl examples:
```bash
# small request
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024-q4","input":"hi"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
# big request (truncated)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024-q4","input":"<3500 tokens>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
```

anna_dev: I also captured the batcher proto dump at spike: `dynbatch.dump()` shows lots of small contexts interleaved with one giant seq.

ingest-bot: Note: customer corp-x has heavy nightly indexing at 02:00 UTC which matches two of the incidents.

sara_support: Actionable plan? Customer is on support tier S. They want a short-term workaround and long term fix.

ben_ml: Short term: create a route override for corp-x that sets `max_batch_size=32`, `coalesce_max_seq=1024`, and `prefer_homogeneous_batches=true`. That should cut tails immediately. Long term: we should add a scheduler policy that groups by request token count and avoid mixing >threshold sizes in same GPU batch. Also add KV cache pressure metrics to the console (eviction_rate, mem_watermark).

mike_sre: I'll open infra ticket INF-7823 to add the routing prefilter and an autoscaling rule that spins a big-worker for heavy seqs so they don't block small-req workers.

anna_dev: Filed reproducer gist and attached logs to support ticket #INC-1234. Notifying customer about temporary route change now.

sara_support: Thanks. Marking as escalated to eng-runtime. Will follow up with customer and record RCA after we confirm. :thumbsup:

mike_sre: quick note for postmortem — check whether the kernel selector incorrectly falls back to a slower path if batch contains mixed seq lengths (we saw a 2x cpu fallback time).

ben_ml: Also add a unit test that simulates interleaved micro/bulk requests for the embeddings batcher.

anna_dev: Will do. For the record, no billing/auth issues here — purely performance and batching behavior.

sara_support: Closing loop: corp-x accepted temporary route change and latency dropped from 800-1200ms to ~45-80ms for small requests. We'll keep monitoring.

[thread ended]"
